central_reading: TĀ 1/181-182 distinguishes two aspects of cognition — objective ascertainment (niścaya: 'this has been perceived') and subjective awareness ('I perceive') — and argues the subjective aspect arises from a prior non-dual consciousness, not from cognition's intrinsic structure. This parallels Dignāga's two-appearance doctrine but with a fundamentally different ontology.
